title: A methodology to characterize bias and harmful stereotypes in natural language processing in Latin America

bias_targets.methodology: Defining a binary bias space using word lists representing masculine and feminine concepts (specifically adapted for morphological gender in Spanish) and analyzing the relative position and similarity of target words within word embeddings.

Constructing a bias space with word lists representing 'Latin American' versus 'North American' identities to measure the relative semantic association of specific professions and stereotypes in the embedding.

Defining an economic bias axis using seed terms related to 'wealthy' (e.g., rich, money) versus 'poor' (e.g., poverty, misery) and exploring how positive and negative sentiment words map onto this axis.

Creating word lists representing 'old' and 'young' concepts to define a bias dimension, and evaluating the relative semantic distances of various verbs and activities (e.g., sleep, dance) to these extremes.
